claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
An Al-containing surface treatment will rapidly form an alumina scale on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature air exposure.
The alumina scale formed on the treated alloy will be continuous, slow-growing, and adherent.
An Al-containing surface treatment will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al-containing surface treatment will not degrade room-temperature tensile ductility.
The Al-containing surface treatment will not degrade yield strength at 1000 °C.
The proposed surface modification will not alter the alloy's as-cast microstructure.
An alumina scale acts as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
The alumina scale will significantly reduce high-temperature oxidation and pesting.
Because the treatment is surface-limited, it will preserve the alloy's bulk microstructure.
Preservation of the bulk microstructure will preserve the alloy's inherent mechanical properties.
After five hours in air, treated samples will have markedly lower oxidation mass gain than untreated samples.
After five hours in air, treated samples will exhibit less oxide spallation than untreated samples.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and is prone to rapid oxidation or pesting at high temperature.
The predicted protection applies in air from 800 °C to 1000 °C for exposures around five hours.
Long-term alumina-scale stability and performance under cyclic thermal loading have not been established.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify exposure for at least five hours, which is open-ended, whereas the boundary confines the prediction to durations around five hours and states that longer-term behavior is unverified.
